rationale: 159-04 discovery (not addressed by the 159-03 decision-of-record): the citing line reads '.../json_parser.c:73-79,113-118' -- a colon_range immediately followed by literal trailing ',113-118' prose (a SECOND range the citation grammar does not actually parse as part of the same match; CITATION_RE only captures '73-79'). 159-03's reviewed answer collapses the range to the single point 133 (disposition hand_choice_retargeted_verbatim, per the operator ruling that only the element type name changed). Rendering 'json_parser.c:133,113-118' is a REAL, semantically inert citation on its first (only intended) apply, but on any SUBSEQUENT re-run CITATION_RE now parses '133,113' as a colon_list with two elements, silently changing the citation's own grammar and re-binding it to a DIFFERENT manifest record shape -- an idempotency hazard, not merely a re-review question, that this phase's file scope and time budget cannot safely resolve by re-authoring the citation prose. Retired rather than risk a grammar-shape regression on re-apply.
